examples.verified_design: Same survey questionnaire has all three hypothetical matchup questions. Random assignment or rotation not documented.
examples.notes: Ossoff advantage: 3 pp margin over Tomlinson, 5 pp over Amico. Ossoff primary was not close; useful quality-measure proof, not a close-primary RD observation.

examples.verified_design: Both general-election matchups in same questionnaire. No documented random assignment.
examples.notes: Norton +3 pp margin over Buck in May. August poll flips ranking; MUST lock time window and aggregation before outcome analysis. The Democratic nomination was also unresolved; a future Bennet win cannot retrospectively choose the common opponent.

examples.verified_design: Same questionnaire all four potential general-election matchups. No documented random assignment.
examples.notes: Field before primary; release on primary morning 10:55AM before tally. Buck +3 pp margin vs Bennet, but Norton +2 pp margin vs Romanoff. Opponent-specific appeal, not universal intrinsic talent. The Democratic nomination was also unresolved; a future Bennet win cannot retrospectively choose the common opponent.

examples.population: Mississippi voters; includes oversample of 422 Republican primary voters
examples.verified_design: Same survey report and questionnaire. No documented random assignment.
examples.notes: Cochran +14 pp comparative margin. Early snapshot; incumbent recognition is part of measured appeal. Must not use July 2014 post-runoff PPP counterfactual poll as pre-treatment. This is outside the proposed 90-day main polling window: measurement feasibility and a 365-day sensitivity candidate, not automatically an eligible main observation.

examples.verified_design: Explicit sequential hypothetical questions in same survey. No documented random assignment.
examples.notes: Perdue +3 pp comparative margin. Conducted AFTER first primary but BEFORE decisive runoff, hence pre-treatment only if treatment is runoff nomination.

examples.mode: Mixed landline, cellphone, and opt-in online
examples.verified_design: Sponsor article reports both hypothetical matchups from same 400 respondent survey. Full question wording or random assignment not confirmed.
examples.notes: Jenkins +4 pp comparative margin. Long pre-primary lead. Do not assume probabilistic margin-of-error for mixed opt-in sample.

examples.verified_design: Both hypothetical matchups in the same survey. No documented random assignment of candidate names or question order.
examples.notes: Booker +5 raw candidate-support points, +6 margin points. Both questions also include Brad Barron at 4%. Poll ends eight days before the primary, so it is outside the old donor study’s 30-day cutoff. General-election poll questions do not establish coattails.

data_map.status: Seven original-source examples; broader archive audit recovered 13 surveys across five nomination cases.
data_map.limitation: Same survey is not randomized assignment; sampling error, recognition, ordering and sparse historical coverage remain. No fitted appeal model.

data_map.source: FEC certified primary and runoff returns + Cowburn annotations
data_map.status: Eight FEC cycles, 2006–2020, inspected for final Senate runoffs; four of 14 final runoffs are within five points. Nine additional conventional-primary candidates plus SC 2008 bring the new-event list to 14.
data_map.limitation: Not a completed expanded analysis cohort. Official dates, exact votes for Cowburn additions, quality availability and special-election coverage still need audit. First-round margins cannot stand in for runoff assignment.

data_map.status: Existing study has pre-primary donor counts for 130 candidate appearances.
data_map.limitation: Train and validate only against pre-primary appeal gaps. Distinct disclosed identities are not all small-dollar donors; old receipt-dated extracts are not complete archival filing vintages.

data_map.source: Official returns; MIT Election Data and Science Lab
data_map.status: House, governor and precinct returns available, with different coverage across years.
data_map.limitation: A statewide nomination is one assignment, even with thousands of precinct rows. Include all districts with verified coverage, flag independents and uncontested races; do not let postnomination contest status choose the sample.

data_map.source: Census citizen voting-age population and population estimates
data_map.status: Historical ACS five-year CVAP files are available below the state level.
data_map.limitation: Use a vintage published before treatment. CVAP approximates the eligible population, not exact legal eligibility. A fixed registered-voter cohort omits induced new registrations.

data_map.source: North Carolina absentee and voter-history files
data_map.status: Actual 2020 absentee file and precinct-by-voting-mode results inspected.
data_map.limitation: Voter history has participation, not secret choices. Mail return date is not necessarily vote date. Early/late voters self-select, so their comparison alone is not a natural experiment.

data_map.status: Published database covers 42.7 million ballots in 20 states and 362 counties.
data_map.limitation: No voting dates or nonvoters; incomplete geographic coverage. It improves outcome measurement, not assignment. Do not link anonymous ballots to identities.

data_map.need: Independent check of an event effect
data_map.source: Candidate shocks with predetermined voting access
data_map.status: Published designs use unexpected campaign shocks and pre-existing early-voting rules.
data_map.limitation: Identifies a particular shock under strong exposure/control assumptions, not the full all-star effect. National and party-brand reactions can be mechanisms; dividing by own-vote changes needs additional assumptions.

archive_scope: Bounded archive audit of 65 old nomination pairs plus nine newly identified conventional-primary cases. Coverage is not a census of available surveys. Additional original sources are separate from archive counts.
causal_estimand: Effect of nominating the candidate with greater measured pre-primary general-election appeal instead of their actual primary rival, among close nominations.
